title: Malaysia approaches universal mobile and internet access while device and place gaps remain
source_unit: Department of Statistics Malaysia, ICT Use and Access by Individuals and Households Survey Report 2025
geography: Malaysia; household ICT access and individual ICT use, including urban-rural and sex comparisons

denominator.unit: households covered by DOSM ICT Use and Access by Individuals and Households Survey; published percentages are survey estimates

household_internet_access.unit: percent of households with Internet access

household_internet_urban.unit: percent of urban households with Internet access

household_internet_rural.unit: percent of rural households with Internet access

urban_rural_gap.unit: percentage-point difference between urban and rural household Internet access

household_computer_access.unit: percent of households with computer access

household_pay_tv_access.unit: percent of households with pay-TV access

mechanism.value: Basic connectivity is close to universal at the national level, but place still marks a meaningful access boundary and the device bundle is changing unevenly

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from DOSM's 2025 ICT Use and Access by Individuals and Households release; urban-rural gap calculated from the published subgroup percentages.
observations.uncertainty: The release reports survey percentages and year-over-year changes, but the summary does not establish service quality, affordability, speed, reliability, computer type, or causal reasons for the urban-rural difference.
observations.subgroup: Malaysian households, with urban and rural subgroup estimates.
observations.counterinterpretation: A high access rate may conceal shared devices, mobile-only access, unstable service, household income differences, or low ability to use services effectively; pay-TV decline may reflect substitution rather than reduced media engagement.

denominator.unit: individuals covered by DOSM ICT Use and Access by Individuals and Households Survey; published percentages are survey estimates

individual_mobile_phone_use.unit: percent of individuals using a mobile phone

individual_internet_use.unit: percent of individuals using the Internet

individual_computer_use.unit: percent of individuals using a computer

internet_use_male.unit: percent of males using the Internet

internet_use_female.unit: percent of females using the Internet

sex_gap.unit: percentage-point difference between male and female Internet use

mobile_computer_gap.unit: percentage-point difference between mobile-phone and computer use

mechanism.value: The dominant consumer interface may be mobile-first: Internet and phone use are nearly universal while computer use remains materially lower

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from DOSM's 2025 ICT Use and Access by Individuals and Households release; device and sex gaps calculated from the published percentages.
observations.uncertainty: These are use indicators, not measures of frequency, task type, digital skill, spending, employment, platform dependence, or outcomes; the sex difference is descriptive and does not establish parity in quality of access.
observations.subgroup: Malaysian individuals, with sex subgroup estimates.
observations.counterinterpretation: Mobile-first use may be an efficient choice rather than a constraint, and the computer-use gap may reflect age, occupation, education, household structure, or device substitution.

boundary: This record adds a Malaysian digital-access and device-configuration layer. It does not establish online shopping, content preferences, digital skills, service quality, affordability, frequency, or causal urban-rural, sex, or device effects.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: DOSM release HTML and linked media statement reviewed; national, urban-rural, device, and sex percentages and year-over-year definitions checked.
